title: B2 · Shape complex accounts and arguments

sources.title: Council of Europe: CEFR Companion Volume (2020)

units.title: Manage viewpoint and time
units.description: Relate a subordinate event to the time of a belief, fear or judgment.

lessons.title: Earlier than a present judgment
lessons.outcome: I can use congiuntivo passato for an event completed before a current viewpoint.
lessons.takeaway: Movement and reflexive verbs use sia plus an agreeing participle.

objectives.label: Earlier than a present judgment
objectives.explanation: After penso che or temo che, use present subjunctive of the auxiliary plus participle for an earlier event. Movement and reflexive verbs use sia plus an agreeing participle.

teach.title: Present viewpoint, earlier event
teach.body: After penso che or temo che, use present subjunctive of the auxiliary plus participle for an earlier event.

examples.it: Penso che Anna abbia già finito.
examples.en: I think Anna has already finished.

teach.title: Choose the right auxiliary
teach.body: Movement and reflexive verbs use sia plus an agreeing participle.

examples.it: Temo che Luca sia partito.
examples.en: I fear Luca has left.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Credo che Marta ___ già arrivata.
questions.translation: I think Marta has already arrived.
questions.explanation: Current credo plus already completed arrival uses sia arrivata.
questions.hint: Use present subjunctive of essere.
questions.speak: Credo che Marta sia già arrivata.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Penso che i ragazzi ___ il treno.
questions.translation: I think the boys missed the train.
questions.explanation: The loss is earlier than the present opinion; use abbiano perso.
questions.hint: Use present subjunctive of avere plus perso.
questions.speak: Penso che i ragazzi abbiano perso il treno.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Temo che loro ___ già usciti.
questions.translation: I fear they have already gone out.
questions.explanation: A current fear about a completed departure takes siano usciti.
questions.hint: Use the present subjunctive auxiliary.
questions.speak: Temo che loro siano già usciti.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: I think Maria understood.
questions.explanation: Abbia capito is earlier than the current belief.
questions.hint: Put the past subjunctive after credo che.
questions.speak: Credo che Maria abbia capito.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: I think she has arrived.
I thought she was arriving.
I thought she had arrived.

questions.explanation: Auxiliary and tense place the arrival before a present or past viewpoint.
questions.hint: Locate the belief in time first.
questions.speak: Penso che sia arrivata.

lessons.title: Contemporary with a past viewpoint
lessons.outcome: I can relate an ongoing event to a belief or feeling in the past.
lessons.takeaway: The imperfect subjunctive keeps the event in the speaker’s viewpoint, without declaring it as a fact.

objectives.label: Contemporary with a past viewpoint
objectives.explanation: Pensavo che or speravo che often takes imperfect subjunctive for a simultaneous or later event viewed from the past. The imperfect subjunctive keeps the event in the speaker’s viewpoint, without declaring it as a fact.

teach.title: Past viewpoint, same time
teach.body: Pensavo che or speravo che often takes imperfect subjunctive for a simultaneous or later event viewed from the past.

examples.it: Pensavo che tu fossi a casa.
examples.en: I thought you were at home.

teach.title: Uncertainty remains
teach.body: The imperfect subjunctive keeps the event in the speaker’s viewpoint, without declaring it as a fact.

examples.it: Speravo che il treno arrivasse in orario.
examples.en: I hoped the train would arrive on time.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Credevo che Luca ___ ancora in ufficio.
questions.translation: I thought Luca was still in the office.
questions.explanation: The office state was simultaneous with the past belief.
questions.hint: Use imperfect subjunctive of essere.
questions.speak: Credevo che Luca fosse ancora in ufficio.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Speravamo che voi ___ con noi.
questions.translation: We hoped you would come with us.
questions.explanation: The hoped-for action was viewed from a past reference point.
questions.hint: Use imperfect subjunctive of venire for voi.
questions.speak: Speravamo che voi veniste con noi.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Temevo che lei non ___ la strada.
questions.translation: I feared she did not know the way.
questions.explanation: The fear and lack of knowledge are aligned in past time.
questions.hint: Use imperfect subjunctive.
questions.speak: Temevo che lei non conoscesse la strada.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: I thought they had time.
questions.explanation: Avessero relates the state to pensavo.
questions.hint: Use the past viewpoint before the clause.
questions.speak: Pensavo che loro avessero tempo.

lessons.title: Earlier than a past viewpoint
lessons.outcome: I can show an event was already over when someone formed a past belief.
lessons.takeaway: With essere, the participle agrees with the subordinate subject.

objectives.label: Earlier than a past viewpoint
objectives.explanation: After a past opinion, use imperfect subjunctive auxiliary plus participle for an even earlier event. With essere, the participle agrees with the subordinate subject.

teach.title: Two points in the past
teach.body: After a past opinion, use imperfect subjunctive auxiliary plus participle for an even earlier event.

examples.it: Pensavo che Anna fosse già partita.
examples.en: I thought Anna had already left.

teach.title: Auxiliary and agreement
teach.body: With essere, the participle agrees with the subordinate subject.

examples.it: Credevo che le ragazze fossero arrivate.
examples.en: I thought the girls had arrived.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Pensavo che Luca ___ già partito.
questions.translation: I thought Luca had already left.
questions.explanation: Earlier departure under past pensavo takes fosse partito.
questions.hint: Use imperfect subjunctive auxiliary.
questions.speak: Pensavo che Luca fosse già partito.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Credevamo che loro ___ il conto.
questions.translation: We thought they had already paid the bill.
questions.explanation: The payment precedes our past belief; use avessero pagato.
questions.hint: Imperfect subjunctive of avere plus participle.
questions.speak: Credevamo che loro avessero già pagato il conto.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Temevo che Maria ___ persa.
questions.translation: I feared Maria had got lost.
questions.explanation: Earlier getting lost under past fear takes si fosse persa.
questions.hint: Use a reflexive pluperfect subjunctive.
questions.speak: Temevo che Maria si fosse persa.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: I hoped Anna had received the letter.
questions.answer: Speravo che Anna avesse ricevuto la lettera.
questions.explanation: Avesse ricevuto places receipt before the past hope.
questions.hint: Use avesse plus the participle.
questions.speak: Speravo che Anna avesse ricevuto la lettera.

lessons.title: Choose the time relationship
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish simultaneous, earlier and later events inside a past viewpoint.
lessons.takeaway: The imperfect subjunctive can also express an event expected later from a past viewpoint, often with a future time marker.

objectives.label: Choose the time relationship
objectives.explanation: Pensavo che fosse in casa refers to then; pensavo che fosse uscito says he had left before then. The imperfect subjunctive can also express an event expected later from a past viewpoint, often with a future time marker.

teach.title: Same time versus earlier
teach.body: Pensavo che fosse in casa refers to then; pensavo che fosse uscito says he had left before then.

examples.it: Credevo che Marco fosse in treno.
examples.en: I thought Marco was on the train.

teach.title: Later from a past point
teach.body: The imperfect subjunctive can also express an event expected later from a past viewpoint, often with a future time marker.

examples.it: Speravo che arrivasse il giorno dopo.
examples.en: I hoped he would arrive the following day.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Alle otto pensavo che Marta ___ ancora al lavoro.
questions.translation: At eight I thought Marta was still at work.
questions.explanation: Ancora al lavoro at eight is simultaneous with the thought.
questions.hint: Choose the simple imperfect subjunctive.
questions.speak: Alle otto pensavo che Marta fosse ancora al lavoro.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Alle otto pensavo che Marta ___ a casa.
questions.translation: At eight I thought Marta had already gone home.
questions.explanation: Già locates her return before the thought at eight.
questions.hint: Use imperfect subjunctive auxiliary plus participle.
questions.speak: Alle otto pensavo che Marta fosse già tornata a casa.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Ieri speravo che Luca ___ oggi.
questions.translation: Yesterday I hoped Luca would arrive today.
questions.explanation: Oggi is later than yesterday’s hope; imperfect subjunctive expresses the expected arrival.
questions.hint: Look at the time marker relative to speravo.
questions.speak: Ieri speravo che Luca arrivasse oggi.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: I thought they had already eaten.
questions.explanation: Già indicates eating before the past belief.
questions.hint: Use the compound subjunctive for earlier time.
questions.speak: Credevo che avessero già mangiato.

units.title: Reflect on unreal outcomes
units.description: Express unreal past situations, regrets and consequences still felt now.

lessons.title: Would have done
lessons.outcome: I can state an unreal past result or polite retrospective judgment.
lessons.takeaway: The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is essere.

objectives.label: Would have done
objectives.explanation: Present conditional of avere or essere plus participle gives would have done. The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is essere.

teach.title: Build the compound conditional
teach.body: Present conditional of avere or essere plus participle gives would have done.

examples.it: Sarei venuta, ma ero malata.
examples.en: I would have come, but I was ill.

teach.title: Agreement with essere
teach.body: The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is essere.

examples.it: Le ragazze sarebbero partite prima.
examples.en: The girls would have left earlier.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Ti ___ chiamato, ma non avevo il numero.
questions.translation: I would have called you, but I did not have the number.
questions.explanation: Avrei chiamato describes a past action that did not happen.
questions.hint: Use conditional of avere.
questions.speak: Ti avrei chiamato, ma non avevo il numero.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Marco ___ venuto, ma lavorava.
questions.translation: Marco would have come, but he was working.
questions.explanation: Venire uses essere in the compound conditional.
questions.hint: Use third-person conditional of essere.
questions.speak: Marco sarebbe venuto, ma lavorava.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Le due amiche ___ rimaste, ma il treno partiva.
questions.translation: The two friends would have stayed, but the train was leaving.
questions.explanation: Rimanere takes essere, and plural subject requires sarebbero rimaste.
questions.hint: Use plural conditional auxiliary.
questions.speak: Le due amiche sarebbero rimaste, ma il treno partiva.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: We would have helped, but we did not know.
questions.answer: Avremmo aiutato, ma non lo sapevamo.
questions.explanation: Avremmo aiutato is a compound conditional of unreal past action.
questions.hint: Put the conditional before the participle.
questions.speak: Avremmo aiutato, ma non lo sapevamo.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: I would have called.
I would call.
I had called.

questions.explanation: The compound conditional differs from a present conditional and a past fact.
questions.hint: Compare avrei, telefonerei and avevo.
questions.speak: Avrei telefonato.

lessons.title: If it had happened
lessons.outcome: I can link an unreal past condition to its unreal past result.
lessons.takeaway: The result normally uses compound conditional.

objectives.label: If it had happened
objectives.explanation: Se plus pluperfect subjunctive marks an unreal past condition. The result normally uses compound conditional.

teach.title: Past condition
teach.body: Se plus pluperfect subjunctive marks an unreal past condition.

examples.it: Se fossimo partiti prima, avremmo preso il treno.
examples.en: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.

teach.title: Past result
teach.body: The result normally uses compound conditional.

examples.it: Se mi avessi scritto, ti avrei risposto.
examples.en: If you had written to me, I would have answered.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Se ___ studiato, avresti superato l’esame.
questions.translation: If you had studied, you would have passed the exam.
questions.explanation: Se introduces the unreal past condition with avessi studiato.
questions.hint: Use pluperfect subjunctive after se.
questions.speak: Se avessi studiato, avresti superato l’esame.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Se fossimo arrivati prima, ___ un posto.
questions.translation: If we had arrived earlier, we would have found a seat.
questions.explanation: The unreal result needs compound conditional avremmo trovato.
questions.hint: Use conditional of avere plus participle.
questions.speak: Se fossimo arrivati prima, avremmo trovato un posto.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Se Anna mi avesse chiamato, ___ andato da lei.
questions.translation: If Anna had called me, I would have gone to her place.
questions.explanation: The unreal result is sarei andato.
questions.hint: Use compound conditional of andare.
questions.speak: Se Anna mi avesse chiamato, sarei andato da lei.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: If it had rained, we would have stayed home.
questions.answer: Se avesse piovuto, saremmo rimasti a casa.
questions.explanation: Avesse piovuto is condition; saremmo rimasti is result.
questions.hint: Order se plus subjunctive before the conditional result.
questions.speak: Se avesse piovuto, saremmo rimasti a casa.

lessons.title: Past cause, present effect
lessons.outcome: I can connect an unreal past event to its consequence now.
lessons.takeaway: Use present conditional for the present consequence and signal now with ora or adesso.

objectives.label: Past cause, present effect
objectives.explanation: Use se plus pluperfect subjunctive for the past event that did not happen. Use present conditional for the present consequence and signal now with ora or adesso.

teach.title: Condition in the past
teach.body: Use se plus pluperfect subjunctive for the past event that did not happen.

examples.it: Se avessi dormito, ora starei meglio.
examples.en: If I had slept, I would feel better now.

teach.title: Result in the present
teach.body: Use present conditional for the present consequence and signal now with ora or adesso.

examples.it: Se avessimo preso il treno, ora saremmo a casa.
examples.en: If we had caught the train, we would be home now.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Se avessi ascoltato, adesso ___ la risposta.
questions.translation: If you had listened, you would know the answer now.
questions.explanation: Adesso makes the result present, so use present conditional.
questions.hint: Look at adesso.
questions.speak: Se avessi ascoltato, adesso sapresti la risposta.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Se avessi preso l’ombrello, ora non ___ bagnato.
questions.translation: If I had taken the umbrella, I would not be wet now.
questions.explanation: The wet state exists now; sarei is present conditional.
questions.hint: Use present conditional of essere.
questions.speak: Se avessi preso l’ombrello, ora non sarei bagnato.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Se fossimo partiti prima, ora ___ già lì.
questions.translation: If we had left earlier, we would already be there now.
questions.explanation: Ora calls for a present conditional result.
questions.hint: Use the simple conditional of essere.
questions.speak: Se fossimo partiti prima, ora saremmo già lì.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: If I had studied, I would understand now.
questions.explanation: A past unreal study leads to a present unreal ability.
questions.hint: Combine past condition with present result.
questions.speak: Se avessi studiato, ora capirei.

units.title: Retell from a later viewpoint
units.description: Shift tense, time and person when reporting past speech or requests.

lessons.title: He said he was leaving
lessons.outcome: I can report a past statement with a past reporting verb.
lessons.takeaway: An action already complete when spoken can become trapassato.

objectives.label: He said he was leaving
objectives.explanation: With disse or ha detto, a simultaneous past claim commonly becomes imperfect in the reported clause. An action already complete when spoken can become trapassato.

teach.title: Shift the viewpoint
teach.body: With disse or ha detto, a simultaneous past claim commonly becomes imperfect in the reported clause.

examples.it: «Sono stanco.» → Ha detto che era stanco.
examples.en: “I am tired.” → He said he was tired.

teach.title: Earlier action
teach.body: An action already complete when spoken can become trapassato.

examples.it: «Ho perso il treno.» → Ha detto che aveva perso il treno.
examples.en: “I missed the train.” → He said he had missed it.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Luca disse: «Sono malato». Luca disse che ___ malato.
questions.translation: Luca said he was ill.
questions.explanation: Era reports a state simultaneous with Luca’s past statement.
questions.hint: Use imperfect indicative for the reported fact.
questions.speak: Luca disse: «Sono malato». Luca disse che era malato.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Anna ha detto: «Ho perso le chiavi». Anna ha detto che ___ le chiavi.
questions.translation: Anna said she had lost the keys.
questions.explanation: Losing the keys came before Anna spoke.
questions.hint: Use trapassato in the reported content.
questions.speak: Anna ha detto: «Ho perso le chiavi». Anna ha detto che aveva perso le chiavi.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Marco disse: «Parto oggi». Marco disse che ___ quel giorno.
questions.translation: Marco said he was leaving that day.
questions.explanation: Partiva relates the departure to the past reporting frame.
questions.hint: Shift the present statement into the past viewpoint.
questions.speak: Marco disse: «Parto oggi». Marco disse che partiva quel giorno.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: He said he had already eaten.
questions.answer: Ha detto che aveva già mangiato.
questions.explanation: Aveva mangiato precedes the moment of saying.
questions.hint: Use che to introduce the reported content.
questions.speak: Ha detto che aveva già mangiato.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: He said he was tired.

pairs.left: Ha detto che aveva perso il treno.
pairs.right: He said he had missed the train.
He said he would leave.

questions.explanation: The subordinate tense shows same time, earlier time or later time than the past report.
questions.hint: Look at era, aveva perso and sarebbe partito.
questions.speak: Ha detto che era stanco.

lessons.title: Retell a question
lessons.outcome: I can report past questions and adjust their reference words.
lessons.takeaway: Keep dove, quando or perché when that is the missing information.

objectives.label: Retell a question
objectives.explanation: A question asked in the past becomes a se clause; the tense and pronouns follow the new viewpoint. Keep dove, quando or perché when that is the missing information.

teach.title: Yes/no with se
teach.body: A question asked in the past becomes a se clause; the tense and pronouns follow the new viewpoint.

examples.it: «Hai fame?» → Mi chiese se avevo fame.
examples.en: “Are you hungry?” → She asked me if I was hungry.

teach.title: Wh word remains
teach.body: Keep dove, quando or perché when that is the missing information.

examples.it: «Dove abiti?» → Mi chiese dove abitavo.
examples.en: “Where do you live?” → She asked where I lived.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Mi chiese: «Vieni domani?» Mi chiese ___ sarei venuto il giorno dopo.
questions.translation: She asked whether I would come the following day.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question becomes a se clause.
questions.hint: Use the word for whether.
questions.speak: Mi chiese: «Vieni domani?» Mi chiese se sarei venuto il giorno dopo.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Mi domandò: «Dove lavori?» Mi domandò dove ___.
questions.translation: She asked where I worked.
questions.explanation: Present lavori shifts to imperfect lavoravo in the past report.
questions.hint: Use imperfect indicative in the new viewpoint.
questions.speak: Mi domandò: «Dove lavori?» Mi domandò dove lavoravo.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Durante il viaggio di ieri Luca chiese: «Quando parte il treno?» Luca chiese quando il treno ___.
questions.translation: Luca asked when the train was leaving.
questions.explanation: The direct present is reported from a past viewpoint with partiva.
questions.hint: Use an indicative imperfect for the timetable.
questions.speak: Durante il viaggio di ieri Luca chiese: «Quando parte il treno?» Luca chiese quando il treno partiva.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: She asked me whether I had seen Maria.
questions.answer: Mi chiese se avevo visto Maria.
questions.explanation: Se introduces the reported yes/no question.
questions.hint: Keep the embedded question inside the statement.
questions.speak: Mi chiese se avevo visto Maria.

lessons.title: Pass on an instruction
lessons.outcome: I can report an instruction with di plus infinitive.
lessons.takeaway: Use the correct indirect object when naming who received the instruction.

objectives.label: Pass on an instruction
objectives.explanation: Dire or chiedere a qualcuno di plus infinitive reports an instruction or request. Use the correct indirect object when naming who received the instruction.

teach.title: Command to another person
teach.body: Dire or chiedere a qualcuno di plus infinitive reports an instruction or request.

examples.it: «Chiudi la porta.» → Mi ha detto di chiudere la porta.
examples.en: “Close the door.” → He told me to close it.

teach.title: Keep the addressee
teach.body: Use the correct indirect object when naming who received the instruction.

examples.it: Ho chiesto a Sara di aspettare.
examples.en: I asked Sara to wait.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Il medico mi ha detto ___ riposare.
questions.translation: The doctor told me to rest.
questions.explanation: Dire a qualcuno di plus infinitive reports the instruction.
questions.hint: Use di before the infinitive.
questions.speak: Il medico mi ha detto di riposare.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Marta ha chiesto a Paolo ___ la finestra.
questions.translation: Marta asked Paolo to open the window.
questions.explanation: Chiedere a qualcuno di plus infinitive reports the request.
questions.hint: Use di plus infinitive.
questions.speak: Marta ha chiesto a Paolo di aprire la finestra.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: «Aspettate qui.» La guida ci ha detto ___ lì.
questions.translation: “Wait here.” The guide told us to wait there.
questions.explanation: Reported instruction after dire uses di aspettare; qui shifts to lì.
questions.hint: Use di plus the infinitive.
questions.speak: «Aspettate qui.» La guida ci ha detto di aspettare lì.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: The boss asked us to arrive early.
questions.answer: Il capo ci ha chiesto di arrivare presto.
questions.explanation: Ci marks the people asked; di introduces the requested action.
questions.hint: Place the recipient before ha chiesto.
questions.speak: Il capo ci ha chiesto di arrivare presto.

units.title: Control agency
units.description: Choose passive form and agreement for what the sentence puts in focus.

lessons.title: Passive across time
lessons.outcome: I can keep passive voice while moving an event across tenses.
lessons.takeaway: For a completed event use essere stato plus participle; agreement follows the subject.

objectives.label: Passive across time
objectives.explanation: Essere plus agreeing participle makes a passive; the auxiliary shows when the action happens. For a completed event use essere stato plus participle; agreement follows the subject.

teach.title: Finite auxiliary carries tense
teach.body: Essere plus agreeing participle makes a passive; the auxiliary shows when the action happens.

examples.it: Il ponte sarà inaugurato domani.
examples.en: The bridge will be opened tomorrow.

teach.title: Completed passive
teach.body: For a completed event use essere stato plus participle; agreement follows the subject.

examples.it: Le lettere sono state inviate ieri.
examples.en: The letters were sent yesterday.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: La mostra ___ aperta domani alle dieci.
questions.translation: The exhibition will be opened tomorrow at ten.
questions.explanation: Domani requires future passive sarà aperta.
questions.hint: Use future essere with feminine participle.
questions.speak: La mostra sarà aperta domani alle dieci.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: I documenti ___ firmati ieri.
questions.translation: The documents were signed yesterday.
questions.explanation: Ieri indicates completed passive; plural documents require sono stati.
questions.hint: Use plural essere stato.
questions.speak: I documenti sono stati firmati ieri.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Quando arrivai, il negozio ___ già stato chiuso.
questions.translation: When I arrived, the shop had already been closed.
questions.explanation: Già and the past reference point require trapassato passive era stato chiuso.
questions.hint: Use imperfect auxiliary before stato.
questions.speak: Quando arrivai, il negozio era già stato chiuso.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: The requests will be examined tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Saranno esaminate agrees with feminine plural richieste.
questions.hint: Use future passive with agreeing participle.
questions.speak: Le richieste saranno esaminate domani.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: The exhibition will be opened tomorrow.

pairs.left: La mostra è stata aperta ieri.
pairs.right: The exhibition was opened yesterday.

pairs.left: La mostra era già stata aperta.
pairs.right: The exhibition had already been opened.

questions.explanation: The passive auxiliary carries the time, while aperta agrees with mostra.
questions.hint: Compare sarà, è stata and era stata.
questions.speak: La mostra sarà aperta domani.

lessons.title: Things are sold here
lessons.outcome: I can use si passivante with a singular or plural thing being acted upon.
lessons.takeaway: A plural thing requires a plural verb in standard Italian.

objectives.label: Things are sold here
objectives.explanation: With a transitive verb and an expressed thing, si passivante makes that thing the grammatical subject. A plural thing requires a plural verb in standard Italian.

teach.title: The thing controls agreement
teach.body: With a transitive verb and an expressed thing, si passivante makes that thing the grammatical subject.

examples.it: Qui si vende il pane.
examples.en: Bread is sold here.

teach.title: Plural thing, plural verb
teach.body: A plural thing requires a plural verb in standard Italian.

examples.it: Qui si vendono libri usati.
examples.en: Used books are sold here.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: In questo negozio si ___ scarpe sportive.
questions.translation: Sports shoes are sold in this shop.
questions.explanation: Scarpe is plural, so si passivante takes vendono.
questions.hint: Let the plural item control the verb.
questions.speak: In questo negozio si vendono scarpe sportive.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Qui si ___ una stanza per l’estate.
questions.translation: A room is rented here for the summer.
questions.explanation: Una stanza is singular, so use si affitta.
questions.hint: Match the singular item.
questions.speak: Qui si affitta una stanza per l’estate.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Su questo sito si ___ molte ricette.
questions.translation: Many recipes can be found on this site.
questions.explanation: Molte ricette is plural, so the verb is trovano.
questions.hint: Match plural ricette.
questions.speak: Su questo sito si trovano molte ricette.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: Books are lent in the library.
questions.explanation: Libri is plural, so si prestano is plural.
questions.hint: Put si before the plural verb.
questions.speak: In biblioteca si prestano libri.

units.title: Compress and refine clauses
units.description: Use precise relatives and shorter infinitive or gerund clauses.

lessons.title: Clarify which noun you mean
lessons.outcome: I can choose il quale or ciò che when a simple che is unclear or has no noun to refer to.
lessons.takeaway: Ciò che means what or the thing that, without an explicit antecedent.

objectives.label: Clarify which noun you mean
objectives.explanation: Il quale and its forms can clarify the noun after a preposition or in a crowded sentence. Ciò che means what or the thing that, without an explicit antecedent.

teach.title: A clearer antecedent
teach.body: Il quale and its forms can clarify the noun after a preposition or in a crowded sentence.

examples.it: Ho parlato con Marta, la quale conosce il direttore.
examples.en: I spoke with Marta, who knows the director.

teach.title: No noun before it
teach.body: Ciò che means what or the thing that, without an explicit antecedent.

examples.it: Non capisco ciò che intendi.
examples.en: I do not understand what you mean.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Ho incontrato le colleghe, ___ mi hanno salutato.
questions.translation: I met the colleagues, who greeted me.
questions.explanation: Le quali agrees with feminine plural colleghe.
questions.hint: Match gender and number to colleghe.
questions.speak: Ho incontrato le colleghe, le quali mi hanno salutato.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Non so ___ desideri davvero.
questions.translation: I do not know what you really want.
questions.explanation: There is no noun antecedent; ciò che means “what.”
questions.hint: Use a relative meaning the thing that.
questions.speak: Non so ciò che desideri davvero.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Ecco il documento sul ___ abbiamo lavorato.
questions.translation: Here is the document on which we worked.
questions.explanation: Sul quale agrees with masculine singular documento; sul cui is not used here.
questions.hint: The article is already in sul; add masculine singular quale.
questions.speak: Ecco il documento sul quale abbiamo lavorato.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: What matters is clarity.
questions.answer: Ciò che conta è la chiarezza.
questions.explanation: Ciò che serves as a noun-free relative subject.
questions.hint: Start with ciò che.
questions.speak: Ciò che conta è la chiarezza.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.left: Le colleghe, le quali conosco, abitano qui.
pairs.right: The colleagues, whom I know, live here.

pairs.left: Il documento sul quale lavoro è pronto.
pairs.right: The document on which I work is ready.

pairs.left: Ciò che conta è la chiarezza.
pairs.right: What matters is clarity.

questions.explanation: Il quale agrees with a noun; ciò che has no explicit noun before it.
questions.hint: Look for the antecedent, then its gender and number.
questions.speak: Le colleghe, le quali conosco, abitano qui.

lessons.title: Shorter clauses with an infinitive
lessons.outcome: I can use an infinitive when the subject relationship is clear.
lessons.takeaway: Aver or essere plus participle can place the infinitive action before the main verb.

objectives.label: Shorter clauses with an infinitive
objectives.explanation: When the subject stays the same, a verb plus infinitive often replaces a full che clause. Aver or essere plus participle can place the infinitive action before the main verb.

teach.title: Same subject
teach.body: When the subject stays the same, a verb plus infinitive often replaces a full che clause.

examples.it: Ho deciso di partire domani.
examples.en: I decided to leave tomorrow.

teach.title: Earlier action with a compound infinitive
teach.body: Aver or essere plus participle can place the infinitive action before the main verb.

examples.it: Dopo aver letto il messaggio, ho risposto.
examples.en: After reading the message, I replied.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Sara ha deciso ___ cambiare lavoro.
questions.translation: Sara decided to change jobs.
questions.explanation: Decidere takes di before a same-subject infinitive.
questions.hint: Learn decidere di as a unit.
questions.speak: Sara ha deciso di cambiare lavoro.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Dopo ___ la mail, ho chiamato Marco.
questions.translation: After reading the email, I called Marco.
questions.explanation: The reading came first and has the same subject as ho chiamato.
questions.hint: Use a compound infinitive after dopo.
questions.speak: Dopo aver letto la mail, ho chiamato Marco.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Prima di uscire, ricordati ___ spegnere la luce.
questions.translation: Before leaving, remember to turn off the light.
questions.explanation: Ricordarsi di plus infinitive is the natural pattern.
questions.hint: Keep the verb’s preposition di.
questions.speak: Prima di uscire, ricordati di spegnere la luce.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: For having replied late, I apologized.
questions.answer: Mi sono scusato per aver risposto tardi.
questions.explanation: Aver risposto puts the reply before the apology.
questions.hint: Use a compound infinitive after per.
questions.speak: Mi sono scusato per aver risposto tardi.

lessons.title: While doing or by doing
lessons.outcome: I can use a gerund when the understood actor is the same.
lessons.takeaway: The gerund can also express how a result is achieved.

objectives.label: While doing or by doing
objectives.explanation: The present gerund can show an action simultaneous with the main one; its subject normally matches. The gerund can also express how a result is achieved.

teach.title: Same actor, overlapping action
teach.body: The present gerund can show an action simultaneous with the main one; its subject normally matches.

examples.it: Camminando, ascoltavo la radio.
examples.en: While walking, I listened to the radio.

teach.title: Method or cause
teach.body: The gerund can also express how a result is achieved.

examples.it: Studiando ogni giorno, farai progressi.
examples.en: By studying every day, you will make progress.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: ___ lungo il fiume, ho incontrato Anna.
questions.translation: While walking along the river, I met Anna.
questions.explanation: The same “I” is walking and meeting; present gerund fits.
questions.hint: Use the -ando form.
questions.speak: Camminando lungo il fiume, ho incontrato Anna.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: ___ con attenzione, capirai meglio.
questions.translation: By listening carefully, you will understand better.
questions.explanation: The same person listens and understands; gerund gives the method.
questions.hint: Use the gerund of ascoltare.
questions.speak: Ascoltando con attenzione, capirai meglio.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: ___ la notizia, Marta è uscita subito.
questions.translation: Having heard the news, Marta left immediately.
questions.explanation: Avendo sentito places the hearing before the departure.
questions.hint: Use a compound gerund for prior action.
questions.speak: Avendo sentito la notizia, Marta è uscita subito.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: While reading the newspaper, I found the advertisement.
questions.answer: Leggendo il giornale, ho trovato l’annuncio.
questions.explanation: The reader and finder are the same subject.
questions.hint: Place gerund clause before main clause.
questions.speak: Leggendo il giornale, ho trovato l’annuncio.

units.title: Build an argument
units.description: Mark contrast, concession and logical progression in connected prose.

lessons.title: Despite the obstacle
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish a factual contrast from a conceded possibility.
lessons.takeaway: Nonostante plus a noun does not need a subordinate verb.

objectives.label: Despite the obstacle
objectives.explanation: Benché or sebbene introduces a conceded fact in a more formal register and takes subjunctive. Nonostante plus a noun does not need a subordinate verb.

teach.title: Benchè with subjunctive
teach.body: Benché or sebbene introduces a conceded fact in a more formal register and takes subjunctive.

examples.it: Benché sia tardi, continuiamo.
examples.en: Although it is late, we continue.

teach.title: Nonostante as a preposition
teach.body: Nonostante plus a noun does not need a subordinate verb.

examples.it: Nonostante la pioggia, siamo usciti.
examples.en: Despite the rain, we went out.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: ___ sia stanco, finirò il lavoro.
questions.translation: Although I am tired, I will finish the work.
questions.explanation: Benché takes the subjunctive sia and signals concession.
questions.hint: Choose the formal although link.
questions.speak: Benché sia stanco, finirò il lavoro.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: ___ il traffico, siamo arrivati puntuali.
questions.translation: Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.
questions.explanation: Nonostante can introduce the noun il traffico directly.
questions.hint: Use a preposition meaning despite.
questions.speak: Nonostante il traffico, siamo arrivati puntuali.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Sebbene ___, siamo usciti.
questions.translation: Although it was raining, we went out.
questions.explanation: Sebbene takes imperfect subjunctive for this past contrast.
questions.hint: Use imperfect subjunctive after sebbene.
questions.speak: Sebbene piovesse, siamo usciti.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: Despite the rain, we went out.
questions.explanation: Nonostante plus the noun phrase states the obstacle.
questions.hint: Put the concession before the main event.
questions.speak: Nonostante la pioggia, siamo usciti.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: Although it is late, we continue.
Despite the rain, we go out.
It is useful; however, it costs a lot.

questions.explanation: Benché introduces a subjunctive clause, nonostante a noun here, tuttavia a counterpoint.
questions.hint: Notice what follows each connector.
questions.speak: Benché sia tardi, continuiamo.

lessons.title: Guide a reader through a claim
lessons.outcome: I can mark an addition, consequence and counterpoint in an argument.
lessons.takeaway: Tuttavia introduces a point that limits or contrasts with the previous one.

objectives.label: Guide a reader through a claim
objectives.explanation: Inoltre adds a point; pertanto or quindi draws a consequence from earlier evidence. Tuttavia introduces a point that limits or contrasts with the previous one.

teach.title: Add and infer
teach.body: Inoltre adds a point; pertanto or quindi draws a consequence from earlier evidence.

examples.it: I costi sono aumentati; pertanto, cambieremo piano.
examples.en: Costs rose; therefore, we will change the plan.

teach.title: Counterpoint
teach.body: Tuttavia introduces a point that limits or contrasts with the previous one.

examples.it: Il progetto è utile; tuttavia, costa troppo.
examples.en: The project is useful; however, it costs too much.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Il servizio è rapido. ___, è gratuito.
questions.translation: The service is fast. Moreover, it is free.
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another benefit; inoltre fits.
questions.hint: Choose an addition link.
questions.speak: Il servizio è rapido. Inoltre, è gratuito.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Il costo è troppo alto; ___, rinunciamo all’acquisto.
questions.translation: The cost is too high; therefore we are giving up the purchase.
questions.explanation: Pertanto presents the decision as a consequence of the cost.
questions.hint: Use the formal therefore link.
questions.speak: Il costo è troppo alto; pertanto, rinunciamo all’acquisto.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Il piano è ambizioso; ___, mancano i fondi.
questions.translation: The plan is ambitious; however, funding is missing.
questions.explanation: The missing funds limit the positive claim; tuttavia signals counterpoint.
questions.hint: Choose a contrast link.
questions.speak: Il piano è ambizioso; tuttavia, mancano i fondi.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: The data are incomplete; therefore caution is needed.
questions.answer: I dati sono incompleti; pertanto, serve cautela.
questions.explanation: Pertanto introduces an inference from the incomplete data.
questions.hint: Place the conclusion after pertanto.
questions.speak: I dati sono incompleti; pertanto, serve cautela.

units.title: Put information in focus
units.description: Change sentence structure to highlight or recover a known topic.

lessons.title: It was Marta who called
lessons.outcome: I can use è...che to focus the person, time or place that matters.
lessons.takeaway: Era can place the focus in a past scene.

objectives.label: It was Marta who called
objectives.explanation: È or era plus the focused element plus che highlights the answer to an implicit question. Era can place the focus in a past scene.

teach.title: Split the sentence for focus
teach.body: È or era plus the focused element plus che highlights the answer to an implicit question.

examples.it: È Marta che ha chiamato, non Luca.
examples.en: It was Marta who called, not Luca.

teach.title: Keep time in the frame
teach.body: Era can place the focus in a past scene.

examples.it: Era ieri che dovevamo partire, non oggi.
examples.en: It was yesterday that we were supposed to leave, not today.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: ___ Paolo che ha prenotato, non Giulia.
questions.translation: It was Paolo who booked, not Giulia.
questions.explanation: È...che highlights Paolo as the corrected person.
questions.hint: Use the cleft opening before the name.
questions.speak: È Paolo che ha prenotato, non Giulia.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: ___ alle otto che parte il treno, non alle nove.
questions.translation: It is at eight that the train leaves, not at nine.
questions.explanation: È...che highlights the corrected departure time.
questions.hint: Open the focus construction with essere.
questions.speak: È alle otto che parte il treno, non alle nove.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: ___ ieri che avevamo appuntamento, non oggi.
questions.translation: It was yesterday that we had an appointment, not today.
questions.explanation: Era...che situates the correction in a past frame.
questions.hint: Use imperfect essere for the past scene.
questions.speak: Era ieri che avevamo appuntamento, non oggi.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: It is Anna who chose the restaurant.
questions.answer: È Anna che ha scelto il ristorante.
questions.explanation: The cleft puts Anna in focus as the chooser.
questions.hint: Place È before the focused name and che after it.
questions.speak: È Anna che ha scelto il ristorante.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: It was Marta who called.
It was yesterday that we left.
That book, I have already read it.

questions.explanation: The first two are clefts highlighting a person or time; the third resumes a fronted topic.
questions.hint: Find the element receiving emphasis.
questions.speak: È Marta che ha chiamato.

lessons.title: Return to a known topic
lessons.outcome: I can put a known object first and resume it with a pronoun.
lessons.takeaway: A prepositional topic can be resumed by ci or ne when it matches the relation.

objectives.label: Return to a known topic
objectives.explanation: Put a known object first, then resume it with a matching direct object clitic in everyday speech. A prepositional topic can be resumed by ci or ne when it matches the relation.

teach.title: Left dislocation
teach.body: Put a known object first, then resume it with a matching direct object clitic in everyday speech.

examples.it: Quel libro, l’ho già letto.
examples.en: That book, I have already read it.

teach.title: Indirect topics
teach.body: A prepositional topic can be resumed by ci or ne when it matches the relation.

examples.it: Di quel problema, ne parliamo domani.
examples.en: That problem, we will talk about it tomorrow.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: La lettera, ___ ho scritta ieri.
questions.translation: The letter, I wrote it yesterday.
questions.explanation: Feminine la becomes l’ before ho and resumes la lettera.
questions.hint: Resume the fronted object with la.
questions.speak: La lettera, l’ ho scritta ieri.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Quei film, ___ abbiamo già visti.
questions.translation: Those films, we have already seen them.
questions.explanation: Li resumes masculine plural quei film; visti agrees.
questions.hint: Use the masculine plural direct object clitic.
questions.speak: Quei film, li abbiamo già visti.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Di questo tema, ___ parleremo domani.
questions.translation: This topic, we will discuss it tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Parlare di takes ne to resume the fronted di phrase.
questions.hint: Keep the relation parlare di.
questions.speak: Di questo tema, ne parleremo domani.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: This book, I know it well.
questions.explanation: Lo resumes the fronted masculine singular object.
questions.hint: Put the topic first and its clitic before the verb.
questions.speak: Questo libro, lo conosco bene.

units.title: Read and tell distant events
units.description: Recognize literary historical narration and the sequence before it.

lessons.title: A completed story event
lessons.outcome: I can recognize and use common passato remoto forms in a written story.
lessons.takeaway: Frequent narrative forms include fu, ebbe, disse, fece, vide and venne.

objectives.label: A completed story event
objectives.explanation: Passato remoto presents a bounded past event as detached from the present. It is common in written narratives; spoken use varies by region. Frequent narrative forms include fu, ebbe, disse, fece, vide and venne.

teach.title: Narrative past
teach.body: Passato remoto presents a bounded past event as detached from the present. It is common in written narratives; spoken use varies by region.

examples.it: Nel 1861 nacque un nuovo Stato.
examples.en: In 1861 a new state was born.

teach.title: Common irregular forms
teach.body: Frequent narrative forms include fu, ebbe, disse, fece, vide and venne.

examples.it: Il re entrò e vide la lettera.
examples.en: The king entered and saw the letter.

questions.prompt: Complete this written story using the passato remoto.
questions.context: Nel racconto, il viaggiatore ___ una porta nascosta.
questions.translation: In the story, the traveler saw a hidden door.
questions.explanation: Vide is a completed literary narrative event in passato remoto.
questions.hint: Use the remote past of vedere.
questions.speak: Nel racconto, il viaggiatore vide una porta nascosta.

questions.prompt: Complete this written story using the passato remoto.
questions.context: Nel 1900 la famiglia ___ a Torino.
questions.translation: In 1900 the family moved to Turin.
questions.explanation: The dated historical event fits passato remoto si trasferì.
questions.hint: Use the remote past of trasferirsi.
questions.speak: Nel 1900 la famiglia si trasferì a Torino.

questions.prompt: Complete this written story using the passato remoto.
questions.context: Il medico ___ la verità e poi uscì.
questions.translation: The doctor told the truth and then left.
questions.explanation: Disse matches the completed sequence marked by poi uscì.
questions.hint: Use remote past of dire.
questions.speak: Il medico disse la verità e poi uscì.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: She entered the room and closed the door.
questions.answer: Entrò nella stanza e chiuse la porta.
questions.explanation: Entrò and chiuse present two bounded literary events.
questions.hint: Keep the narrative verbs in sequence.
questions.speak: Entrò nella stanza e chiuse la porta.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: The traveler saw a light, a bounded story event.
The traveler could see a light, a story background.

pairs.left: Il viaggiatore aveva già visto la luce.
pairs.right: The traveler had already seen the light before that past point.

questions.explanation: Vide narrates an event; vedeva describes background; aveva visto is earlier.
questions.hint: Compare the simple remote, imperfect and trapassato forms.
questions.speak: Il viaggiatore vide una luce.

lessons.title: Before a remote past event
lessons.outcome: I can recognize trapassato remoto in a written historical sequence.
lessons.takeaway: This tense is rare in everyday conversation; recognize it in formal or literary written Italian.

objectives.label: Before a remote past event
objectives.explanation: In literary narration, trapassato remoto marks an action completed immediately before a passato remoto event, often after appena or non appena. This tense is rare in everyday conversation; recognize it in formal or literary written Italian.

teach.title: A prior completed event
teach.body: In literary narration, trapassato remoto marks an action completed immediately before a passato remoto event, often after appena or non appena.

examples.it: Appena ebbe finito, uscì.
examples.en: As soon as he had finished, he went out.

teach.title: Reading priority
teach.body: This tense is rare in everyday conversation; recognize it in formal or literary written Italian.

examples.it: Appena fu arrivata, la chiamarono.
examples.en: When she had arrived, they called her.

questions.prompt: Complete this literary sequence using the trapassato remoto.
questions.context: Appena ___ finito di parlare, il pubblico applaudì.
questions.translation: As soon as he had finished speaking, the audience applauded.
questions.explanation: Ebbe finito is trapassato remoto before applaudì.
questions.hint: Use remote past of avere as auxiliary.
questions.speak: Appena ebbe finito di parlare, il pubblico applaudì.

questions.prompt: Complete this literary sequence using the trapassato remoto.
questions.context: Non appena Anna ___ uscita, il telefono squillò.
questions.translation: As soon as Anna had gone out, the phone rang.
questions.explanation: Fu uscita is trapassato remoto with essere.
questions.hint: Use remote past of essere.
questions.speak: Non appena Anna fu uscita, il telefono squillò.

questions.prompt: Complete this literary sequence using the trapassato remoto.
questions.context: Quando i ragazzi ___ partiti, iniziò a piovere.
questions.translation: When the boys had left, it began to rain.
questions.explanation: Furono partiti places the completed departure just before iniziò.
questions.hint: Use plural remote auxiliary.
questions.speak: Quando i ragazzi furono partiti, iniziò a piovere.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: As soon as she had closed the door, she left.
questions.answer: Appena ebbe chiuso la porta, partì.
questions.explanation: Ebbe chiuso precedes the next remote past event.
questions.hint: Put the completed prior action after appena.
questions.speak: Appena ebbe chiuso la porta, partì.
